awareness.eyebrow: A LITTLE KNOWLEDGE GOES A LONG WAY
awareness.title: Get to know the air around you.
awareness.description: Understand the number. Look beyond the color. Learn where the data comes from.
aqiGuideTitle: A number with a little more meaning.
aqiGuideBody: US AQI groups air quality into six categories. Higher values indicate greater air-pollution concern. Labels and symbols accompany every color in Aero Health.
pollutantGuideBody: Our sample views separate PM2.5, PM10, ozone, nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide. Their units and source matter as much as their values.
sourceGuideTitle: A clearer source. A clearer picture.
sourceGuideBody: An official source, a community sample and a model estimate are different kinds of evidence. Check the timestamp and avoid treating a nearby station as a measurement at your exact location.
articleLanguage: Extended educational references are in English.
faq1a: Not in the default demo. All sample readings, provider assignments and forecasts are fictional. Switch to real mode only after integrating and checking your backend.
faq2: Why do some areas have no data?
faq2a: A nearby reading is not the same as a local measurement. Areas without a sample display no direct data and identify the nearest available station separately.
faq3: Does purple mean the worst air quality?
faq3a: Purple identifies very unhealthy conditions on the US AQI scale. The additional hazardous category uses a deeper maroon tone. The full six-category scale is retained here.
faq4: Does Aero Health give medical advice?
faq4a: No. The advisory screen demonstrates explainable rules using fictional readings and optional example profiles. It is not a diagnosis or a treatment recommendation.
